meta.title: Faith and epic journeys
methodology: Every verse is copied verbatim from the public page named in its 'verified from' link (Wikisource, SuttaCentral, BaniDB or the Valmiki and Mahabharata pages already used for the epic atlas); English translations are our own.
Where a stage or stop has no verse we could check for that exact place, we show a verified verse from the same text and label it 'From the text (general)'.
Places for ancient and traditional events are approximate identifications, not surveyed sites; stops marked approximate are drawn with a dashed ring.
Borders are a cartographic convention for orientation; the basemap is Natural Earth (public domain) with India drawn from the Survey of India outline.
Prakrit Jain canonical texts could not be checked against an online edition, so Mahavira's stops use the Sanskrit Tattvartha Sutra.

journeys.title: The Vedas and Upanishads: where the texts took shape
journeys.subtitle: From the northwestern tributaries and Sapta-Sindhu across the Gangetic courts to the classical commentarial mathas
journeys.intro: Vedic geography is reconstructed from the texts themselves and from later tradition, so every pin is a scholarly or traditional identification, not a surveyed site.

routes.label: Vedic & Upanishadic heartlands
routes.summary: Fifteen stages tracking the eastward geographical horizon from Rigvedic Punjab rivers to the Upanishadic courts and southern commentarial seats.

stops.name: Gandhara & Western Tributaries (Kubha–Suvastu)
stops.description: Early hymns in the Rigveda name the Kabul (Kubha), Swat (Suvastu) and Kurram rivers alongside Gandhara wool and mountain passes.

quote.translation: Gather, Ganga, Yamuna, Sarasvati, Shutudri, round this my song of praise, together with Parushni.
quote.label: From the text (general)

stops.name: Sapta-Sindhu (Central Punjab Doabs)
stops.description: The Rigveda keeps returning to the seven rivers of the north-west. The Nadistuti lists them from east to west in solemn praise.

stops.description: Rigveda 3.33 stages Vishvamitra’s famed poetic dialogue asking the roaring Beas and Sutlej rivers to lower their floodwaters for crossing.

quote.text: प्र पर्वतानामुशती उपस्थादश्वे इव विषिते हासमाने । गावेव शुभ्रे मातरा रिहाणे विपाट् छुतुद्री पयसा जवेते

stops.name: Sarasvati valley and Kurukshetra
stops.description: Middle and late Vedic ritual is anchored between the Sarasvati and Drishadvati in Bharata–Kuru territory; Dirghatamas’s riddle hymn declares that truth is one.

quote.text: एकं सद्विप्रा बहुधा वदन्त्यग्निं यमं मातरिश्वानमाहुः

stops.name: Hastinapura & the Upper Doab
stops.description: Painted Grey Ware levels and later Vedic Yajurveda recensions shift the political centre of gravity into the upper Ganga–Yamuna doab.

stops.name: Kampilya (Kuru–Panchala country)

routes.label: The Buddha’s life
routes.summary: Sixteen canonical sites from birth at Lumbini and awakening at Bodh Gaya to the last meal at Pava and parinirvana at Kushinagar.

stops.name: Lumbini
stops.description: Born in the gardens of Lumbini, in today’s Nepal. The Acchariyabbhutasutta pictures the newborn standing firm and taking seven strides.

quote.text: ‘sampatijāto, ānanda, bodhisatto samehi pādehi pathaviyaṁ patiṭṭhahitvā uttarābhimukho sattapadavītihārena gacchati, setamhi chatte anudhāriyamāne, sabbā ca disā viloketi, āsabhiñca vācaṁ bhāsati—aggohamasmi lokassa, jeṭṭhohamasmi lokassa, seṭṭhohamasmi lokassa. Ayamantimā jāti, natthi dāni punabbhavo’ti.
quote.translation: ‘As soon as he was born, Ananda, the Bodhisatta stood firm on level feet, faced north, took seven strides with a white parasol held over him, looked in every direction and spoke these bull-like words: “I am the foremost in the world, I am the eldest in the world, I am the best in the world. This is my last birth; now there is no more rebirth.”’

stops.name: Kapilavastu
stops.description: Capital of the Sakyan republic where Siddhattha grew up, and where he later returned to teach his clan.

quote.text: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sakkesu viharati kapilavatthusmiṁ nigrodhārāme.
quote.translation: At one time the Buddha was staying among the Sakyans at Kapilavatthu, in the Banyan Tree Monastery.

stops.name: Anupiya (Crossing into homelessness)
stops.description: Traditional border mango grove beyond the Anoma river where Siddhattha cut his hair and became a wandering ascetic.

quote.text: “Pabbajjaṁ kittayissāmi, yathā pabbaji cakkhumā; Yathā vīmaṁsamāno so, pabbajjaṁ samarocayi.
quote.translation: I shall tell of the going forth — how the one with vision went forth, how he reflected and came to approve of the going forth.
quote.label: From the text (general)

stops.name: Rajagriha (Bimbisara & Venuvana)
stops.description: Magadhan hill capital where young Siddhattha first met King Bimbisara, and later taught at the Bamboo Grove (Venuvana).

quote.text: “Pabbajjaṁ kittayissāmi, yathā pabbaji cakkhumā; Yathā vīmaṁsamāno so, pabbajjaṁ samarocayi.
quote.translation: I shall tell of the going forth — how the one with vision went forth, how he reflected and came to approve of the going forth.

stops.name: Bodh Gaya (Uruvela, River Neranjara)
stops.description: Beneath the Bodhi tree beside the Neranjara river he attained awakening, recounted in Udana 1.1 and the Dhammapada.

quote.text: Evaṁ me sutaṁ— ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā uruvelāyaṁ viharati najjā nerañjarāya tīre bodhirukkhamūle paṭhamābhisambuddho.
quote.translation: So I have heard. At one time the Buddha was staying near Uruvela on the bank of the river Neranjara at the foot of the Bodhi tree, having just attained awakening.

stops.name: Gaya Head (Gayashisha)
stops.description: On the rocky hill above Gaya he preached the Adittapariyayasutta (‘Everything is burning’) to a thousand converted ascetics.

quote.text: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā gayāyaṁ viharati gayāsīse saddhiṁ bhikkhusahassena. Tatra kho bhagavā bhikkhū āmantesi: “sabbaṁ, bhikkhave, ādittaṁ.
quote.translation: At one time the Buddha was staying at Gaya on Gaya Head with a thousand mendicants. There he addressed the mendicants: “Mendicants, everything is burning.”

stops.name: Sarnath (Isipatana)
stops.description: In the deer park at Isipatana he delivered the Dhammacakkappavattana Sutta, teaching the Middle Way to his five companions.

quote.text: “Dveme, bhikkhave, antā pabbajitena na sevitabbā.
quote.translation: These two extremes, monks, are not to be followed by one who has gone forth.

stops.name: Varanasi (Yasa & First Sangha)
stops.description: Nearby Varanasi saw the conversion of Yasa and his friends, forming the first mission sent out ‘for the welfare of the many’.

quote.text: Caratha, bhikkhave, cārikaṁ bahujanahitāya bahujanasukhāya lokānukampāya atthāya hitāya sukhāya devamanussānaṁ.
quote.translation: Wander forth, monks, for the good of the many, for the happiness of the many, out of compassion for the world, for the benefit, good and happiness of gods and humans.

stops.name: Nalanda (Pavarika’s Mango Grove)
stops.description: Travelling between Rajagaha and Nalanda frames the Brahmajala Sutta; later centuries raised Nalanda into a great monastic university.

quote.text: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā antarā ca rājagahaṁ antarā ca nāḷandaṁ addhānamaggappaṭipanno hoti mahatā bhikkhusaṅghena saddhiṁ pañcamattehi bhikkhusatehi.
quote.translation: At one time the Buddha was travelling on the road between Rajagaha and Nalanda with a large Sangha of about five hundred monks.

stops.name: Kosambi (Ghositarama Monastery)
stops.description: Capital of Vamsa/Vatsa on the Yamuna, where the Buddha stayed at Ghositarama to reconcile arguing mendicants.

quote.text: Evaṁ me sutaṁ— ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā kosambiyaṁ viharati ghositārāme.
quote.translation: So I have heard. At one time the Buddha was staying near Kosambi in Ghosita’s Monastery.

stops.name: Shravasti (Jetavana)
stops.description: Anathapindika’s Jetavana park in Kosala hosted more canonical suttas and rainy-season retreats than any other site.

quote.text: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā sāvatthiyaṁ viharati jetavane anāthapiṇḍikassa ārāme.
quote.translation: At one time the Buddha was staying near Shravasti in Jeta’s Grove, Anathapindika’s monastery.

stops.name: Sankasya (Sankissa)
stops.description: Famed in later pilgrimage accounts (Faxian and Xuanzang) as an early monumental stupa centre of Madhyadesha.

quote.text: Sabbapāpassa akaraṇaṁ, kusalassa upasampadā; Sacittapariyodapanaṁ, etaṁ buddhāna sāsanaṁ.
quote.translation: To avoid all evil, to undertake the good, to purify one’s own mind: this is the teaching of the Buddhas.
quote.label: From the text (general)

stops.name: Pataligama (Pataliputra crossing)
stops.description: Crossing the Ganga near the new Magadhan fortress, the Buddha prophesied Pataligama would rise into a foremost city.

quote.text: Tena kho pana samayena sunidhavassakārā magadhamahāmattā pāṭaligāme nagaraṁ māpenti vajjīnaṁ paṭibāhāya.
quote.translation: Now at that time the Magadhan ministers Sunidha and Vassakara were building a city at Pataligama to hold back the Vajjis.

stops.name: Vaishali (Mahavana & Capala Shrine)
stops.description: Republic of the Licchavis; in his final year the Buddha praised Vaishali’s shrines and announced his approaching parinirvana.

quote.text: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā vesāliyaṁ viharati mahāvane kūṭāgārasālāyaṁ.
quote.translation: At one time the Buddha was staying near Vaishali in the Great Wood, in the hall with the peaked roof.

stops.name: Pava (Cunda’s Mango Grove)
stops.description: At Pava in Malla territory the Buddha stayed at Cunda the smith’s mango grove and ate his last meal before walking to Kushinagar.

quote.text: Tatra sudaṁ bhagavā pāvāyaṁ viharati cundassa kammāraputtassa ambavane.
quote.translation: And there the Buddha stayed near Pava in the mango grove of Cunda the smith’s son.

stops.name: Kushinagar (Upavattana Sal Grove)
stops.description: Between twin sal trees on the Hiranyavati river, he left his last charge: ‘Conditioned things decay; strive on with diligence.’

quote.text: vayadhammā saṅkhārā, appamādena sampādetha.
quote.translation: Conditioned things are bound to decay; strive on with diligence.

routes.label: Spread of Buddhism
routes.summary: Fifteen hubs tracking overland Silk Road, Himalayan, East Asian and maritime transmissions.

stops.name: Pataliputra (Ashokan Heartland)
stops.description: Emperor Ashoka’s imperial capital: chronicles record the Third Council and diplomatic Dharma missions dispatched outward.

stops.name: Sanchi & Vidisha (Central India)
stops.description: Starting point for Ashoka’s children Mahinda and Sanghamitta according to Sri Lankan chronicles; home to Ashoka’s Great Stupa.

quote.text: Santi, bhante, aññāni mahānagarāni, seyyathidaṁ— campā rājagahaṁ sāvatthī sāketaṁ kosambī bārāṇasī;
quote.translation: “Venerable sir, there are other great cities — namely Champa, Rajagriha, Shravasti, Saketa, Kosambi and Varanasi;”
quote.label: From the text (general)

stops.name: Anuradhapura (Sri Lanka)
stops.description: Sri Lankan chronicles trace Theravada transmission and the Mahabodhi sapling here under King Devanampiya Tissa.

stops.name: Amaravati & Nagarjunakonda (Andhra)
stops.description: Krishna valley monasteries where Mahasanghika schools, marble stupas and early Prajnaparamita traditions flourished.

stops.description: Kushan and Gandharan workshops pioneered anthropomorphic Buddha sculpture and northwest Kharoshthi manuscripts.

stops.description: Caravan monastery crossroads famous for two colossal cliff-carved Buddhas along the road linking Bactria and India.

stops.description: Southern Silk Road oasis kingdoms preserving Prakrit, Khotanese Saka and Sanskrit manuscripts across the Taklamakan desert.

stops.description: Oasis gateway into China famed for hundreds of painted cave shrines and the sealed Library Cave of multilingual scriptures.

stops.description: Early imperial translation centre anchored in tradition by the White Horse Temple of 68 CE.

stops.description: Buddhism entered the Korean peninsula from northern China, inspiring Bulguksa and Seokguram grotto.

stops.name: Nara (Japan)
stops.description: Transmitted via Korea and Tang China; Nara’s Todai-ji houses the monumental bronze Vairocana Buddha.

quote.translation: Through many births I wandered in samsara, seeking but not finding the builder of the house; painful is birth again and again.
quote.label: From the text (general)

stops.name: Lhasa (Tibetan Plateau)
stops.description: Shantarakshita, Padmasambhava and later masters like Atisha brought late Indian monastic scholarship across the Himalaya.

stops.description: Pala monastic universities sent scholars (such as Atisha Dipankara) directly to Tibet and maritime Southeast Asia.

stops.name: Bagan (Myanmar)
stops.description: On the Irrawaddy plain Burmese monarchs raised over two thousand brick stupas supporting Theravada learning.

stops.name: Borobudur (Central Java)
stops.description: Shailendra kings built the world’s largest Buddhist stepped mandala monument in volcanic stone on Java.

journeys.subgroup: Mahavira: A Teacher on the Road
journeys.title: Mahavira: a teacher on the road
journeys.subtitle: Fourteen stages of Mahavira’s wanderings across Bihar, Bengal and Kosala, plus ten historic Jain centres across India
journeys.intro: Dates and sites follow Jain tradition (c. 6th century BCE) and several are disputed, so pins are approximate. Because Prakrit canonical texts were not fetched online here, verses use the Sanskrit Tattvartha Sutra (general).

routes.label: Mahavira’s wanderings
routes.summary: Fourteen stops following the Kalpa Sutra itinerary from Vaishali through Radha and Anga to kevala jnana and Pavapuri.

stops.name: Kundagrama (Vaishali area)
stops.description: Born to King Siddhartha and Queen Trishala of the Jnatri clan. Svetambara and Digambara traditions preserve distinct nearby locations.

quote.text: तत्त्वार्थश्रद्धानं सम्यग्दर्शनम्।।
quote.translation: Faith in the realities as they are is right view.
quote.label: From the text (general)

stops.name: Jnatrkhanda grove
stops.description: At thirty he stepped away from princely life beneath an ashoka tree and adopted complete renunciation.

quote.text: हिंसाऽनृतस्तेयाब्रह्मपरिग्रहेभ्यो विरतिर्व्रतम्
quote.translation: Abstaining from violence, falsehood, theft, unchastity and possessiveness is the set of vows.
quote.label: From the text (general)

stops.name: Kollaga / Karmaragrama
stops.description: Kalpa Sutra records his earliest wanderings in the northern Vajjian countryside near Vaishali.

quote.text: सम्यग्दर्शन ज्ञान चारित्राणि मोक्षमार्गः।।
quote.translation: Right view, right knowledge and right conduct together are the path to liberation.
quote.label: From the text (general)

stops.name: Asthikagrama (Early austerities)
stops.description: Named among his first rainy-season retreats as he travelled southward into Jharkhand and eastern plains.

quote.text: प्रमत्तयोगात्प्राणव्यपरोपणं हिंसा
quote.translation: Violence is the taking of life through careless activity.
quote.label: From the text (general)

stops.name: Radha (Western Bengal paths)
stops.description: Acharanga Sutra describes arduous wanderings through pathless Radha country enduring silence, fasting and hostility.

quote.text: प्रमत्तयोगात्प्राणव्यपरोपणं हिंसा
quote.translation: Violence is the taking of life through careless activity.
quote.label: From the text (general)

stops.name: Nalanda
stops.description: Tradition recounts a rainy-season stay near Nalanda and his philosophical encounter with Makkhali Gosala.

quote.text: प्रमत्तयोगात्प्राणव्यपरोपणं हिंसा
quote.translation: Violence is the taking of life through careless activity.
quote.label: From the text (general)

stops.name: Champa (Capital of Anga)
stops.description: Repeatedly honoured in the Kalpa Sutra and Aupapatika Sutra as a major river port supporting the early Sangha.

quote.text: परस्परोपग्रहो जीवानाम्।।
quote.translation: Living beings render support to one another.
quote.label: From the text (general)

stops.name: Mithila (Videha)
stops.description: Kalpa Sutra attributes six rainy-season retreats to ancient Mithila and Vaishali regions.

quote.text: तत्त्वार्थश्रद्धानं सम्यग्दर्शनम्।।
quote.translation: Faith in the realities as they are is right view.
quote.label: From the text (general)

stops.name: Varanasi (Legacy of Parshvanatha)
stops.description: Traditional birthplace of the 23rd Tirthankara Parshvanatha, whose fourfold restraint (chaturyama) preceded Mahavira’s reform.

quote.text: हिंसाऽनृतस्तेयाब्रह्मपरिग्रहेभ्यो विरतिर्व्रतम्
quote.translation: Abstaining from violence, falsehood, theft, unchastity and possessiveness is the set of vows.
quote.label: From the text (general)

stops.name: Shravasti
stops.description: Northern Kosala city where lay patrons like Ananda and Kundakoliya welcomed Mahavira and his ganadharas.

quote.text: सम्यग्दर्शन ज्ञान चारित्राणि मोक्षमार्गः।।
quote.translation: Right view, right knowledge and right conduct together are the path to liberation.
quote.label: From the text (general)

stops.name: Kaushambi (Vatsa capital)
stops.description: Tradition links Kaushambi with Queen Mrigavati and fasts of Chandanabala, first head of the Jain nuns.

quote.text: मैत्री-प्रमोद-कारुण्य-माध्यस्थानि च सत्त्व-गुणाधिक-क्लिश्यमानाविनेयेषु
quote.translation: Friendship, delight in the virtuous, compassion for the suffering, and equanimity toward the unruly — these are to be cultivated towards all beings.
quote.label: From the text (general)

stops.name: Jrimbhikagrama (Rijuvalika bank)
stops.description: After twelve years of penance he attained kevala jnana on the bank of the Rijupalika; the exact modern bank is debated.

quote.translation: From the destruction of delusion, and of the karmas that obscure knowledge and perception and that obstruct, omniscience (kevala) arises.
quote.note: Tattvartha Sutra 10.1 defines omniscience; it is not a text of this place.

stops.name: Rajagriha (Vipulachala Hill)
stops.description: Fourteen rainy seasons in the Magadhan capital; Indrabhuti Gautama became chief disciple and King Shrenika heard his sermons.

quote.text: मैत्री-प्रमोद-कारुण्य-माध्यस्थानि च सत्त्व-गुणाधिक-क्लिश्यमानाविनेयेषु
quote.translation: Friendship, delight in the virtuous, compassion for the suffering, and equanimity toward the unruly — these are to be cultivated towards all beings.
quote.label: From the text (general)

stops.name: Pavapuri (Jal Mandir)
stops.description: Attained final moksha on the night remembered at Diwali by Jains; marked today by the white marble lake shrine.

quote.text: बन्धहेत्व भावनिर्जराभ्यां कृत्स्न कर्मविप्रमोक्षो मोक्षः।।
quote.translation: With no new cause of bondage and with the shedding of the old, the total release from karma is liberation.
quote.label: From the text (general)

routes.label: Spread of Jain centres across India

stops.description: Rashtrakuta rock-cut monoliths excavated into Sahyadri basalt alongside Buddhist and Hindu caves.

stops.name: Mudabidri (Dakshina Kashi)
stops.description: Known for the Thousand-Pillar Basadi and palm-leaf manuscripts of the Dhavala and Shatkhandagama preserved in coastal Karnataka.

quote.text: बन्धहेत्व भावनिर्जराभ्यां कृत्स्न कर्मविप्रमोक्षो मोक्षः।।
quote.translation: With no new cause of bondage and with the shedding of the old, the total release from karma is liberation.
quote.label: From the text (general)

journeys.title: The ten Sikh Gurus’ journeys
journeys.subtitle: From Guru Nanak’s four udasis and the Punjab seats of Gurus Angad–Har Krishan to Guru Tegh Bahadur and Guru Gobind Singh at Nanded
journeys.intro: Verses are Gurmukhi text from the Guru Granth Sahib via BaniDB. Four Gurus (Hargobind, Har Rai, Har Krishan, Gobind Singh) have no hymn in it, so their stops use a verse by another author and say so.

routes.label: Guru Nanak (1469–1539)
routes.summary: Nineteen key stages across his four long udasis (east, south, north and west) ending in the communal farm at Kartarpur.

stops.name: Talwandi (Nankana Sahib)
stops.description: Born at Rai Bhoi di Talwandi (now Nankana Sahib in Punjab, Pakistan); Janamsakhis recount his early Sacha Sauda hospitality.

quote.label: From the text (general)

stops.name: Sultanpur Lodhi
stops.description: Served as keeper of the state granary; after three days at the Kali Bein stream he proclaimed his universal message.

quote.text: ੴ ਸਤਿ ਨਾਮੁ ਕਰਤਾ ਪੁਰਖੁ ਨਿਰਭਉ ਨਿਰਵੈਰੁ ਅਕਾਲ ਮੂਰਤਿ ਅਜੂਨੀ ਸੈਭੰ ਗੁਰ ਪ੍ਰਸਾਦਿ ॥

quote.note: Sites and order follow the Janamsakhi tradition; accounts differ.

stops.name: Saidpur (Eminabad)
stops.description: Guest of honest carpenter Bhai Lalo rather than Malik Bhago; later composed Baburvani verses here naming Bhai Lalo.

quote.text: ਜੈਸੀ ਮੈ ਆਵੈ ਖਸਮ ਕੀ ਬਾਣੀ ਤੈਸੜਾ ਕਰੀ ਗਿਆਨੁ ਵੇ ਲਾਲੋ ॥

quote.note: Sites and order follow the Janamsakhi tradition; accounts differ.

stops.name: Kurukshetra
stops.description: Questioned empty ritual and meat/superstition taboos before assembled pilgrims at the solar eclipse fair.

stops.description: Engaged Sheikh Sharaf and Sufi pir lineages along the grand trunk road southward.

stops.description: Met Sultan Sikandar Lodi and healed humble devotees along the Yamuna ferry.

stops.name: Haridwar
stops.description: Famously tossed Ganga water westward toward his fields in Punjab to show the futility of throwing water to the sun.

quote.label: From the text (general)
quote.note: Sites and order follow the Janamsakhi tradition; accounts differ.

stops.name: Nanakmatta (Uttarakhand)
stops.description: Debated Siddha Nath yogis at Gorakhmata, now honoured as Gurdwara Sri Nanakmatta Sahib.

stops.description: Sang of inner light rather than funerary clay lamps during pind ceremonies along the Phalgu.

stops.description: Puratan Janamsakhi traditions recall his preaching in Bengal before turning southward along the coast.

stops.description: Tradition sets his soaring cosmic Aarti (‘Gagan mai thaal’) before the temple rituals at Puri.

stops.description: Tradition says a spring of sweet water gushed from the parched hillside at Nanak Jhira as he travelled across the Deccan.

stops.description: Southernmost Indian stage preceding his sea voyage to Jaffna and Kandy in Janamsakhi accounts.

stops.description: Siddh Gosht preserves his sustained verse dialogue with Himalayan yogis on spiritual detachment in worldly life.

stops.description: Janamsakhis relate the famous episode where he slept with feet toward the Kaaba to teach that God’s house fills every direction.

quote.label: From the text (general)
quote.note: Sites and order follow the Janamsakhi tradition; accounts differ.

stops.name: Baghdad (Iraq)
stops.description: Met Pir Bahlol beside the Tigris and spoke of countless hundreds of thousands of worlds; a 16th-century shrine inscription exists here.

quote.note: Sites and order follow the Janamsakhi tradition; accounts differ.

stops.name: Kartarpur (River Ravi)
stops.description: Founded a model farming community uniting honest labour (kirat), shared langar and daily worship, and appointed Bhai Lehna as Guru Angad.

quote.text: ਘਾਲਿ ਖਾਇ ਕਿਛੁ ਹਥਹੁ ਦੇਇ ॥ ਨਾਨਕ ਰਾਹੁ ਪਛਾਣਹਿ ਸੇਇ ॥੧॥
quote.translation: One who earns by honest labour and gives something away from his own hand — says Nanak, that person knows the way.

routes.label: Guru Angad (1504–1552)
routes.summary: Seven places tracing Bhai Lehna from Matte di Sarai and Kartarpur service to Khadur Sahib’s Gurmukhi primer and Mal Akhara.

stops.name: Matte di Sarai (Sri Muktsar Sahib)
stops.description: Born Lehna at Matte di Sarai in a Trehan Khatri merchant household before his family relocated during Babur’s raids.

quote.label: From the text (general)

stops.name: Sanghar & Harike (Beas–Sutlej crossing)

stops.name: Kartarpur (Serving Guru Nanak)
stops.description: On hearing Bhai Jodha recite Japji, Lehna travelled to Kartarpur, passed humble trials of service and received the name Angad (‘my own limb’).

stops.description: Organised daily physical wrestling (Mal Akhara) beside Mata Khivi’s famed community kitchen serving wholesome food to all castes.

routes.summary: Fourteen places from Patna Sahib and Paonta’s literary court to Anandpur’s Khalsa creation, Chamkaur, Damdama and Nanded.

stops.name: Patna Sahib
stops.description: Born Gobind Rai in Patna, Bihar, while his father Guru Tegh Bahadur travelled across Bengal and Assam.

quote.text: ਭੈ ਕਾਹੂ ਕਉ ਦੇਤ ਨਹਿ ਨਹਿ ਭੈ ਮਾਨਤ ਆਨ ॥ ਕਹੁ ਨਾਨਕ ਸੁਨਿ ਰੇ ਮਨਾ ਗਿਆਨੀ ਤਾਹਿ ਬਖਾਨਿ ॥੧੬॥
quote.translation: One who neither frightens anyone nor is frightened by anyone — says Nanak, listen, O mind: call such a person wise.
quote.citation: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 1427 (shalok of Guru Tegh Bahadur)
quote.label: From the text (general)
quote.note: This Guru has no hymn in the Guru Granth Sahib; the verse is by Guru Tegh Bahadur and chosen to illustrate the theme, not attributed to this Guru.

stops.name: Lakhnaur Sahib (Near Ambala)
stops.description: Childhood stop during the family’s march back from Patna to Anandpur; met Muslim saint Sayyid Bhikhan Shah.

quote.text: ਭੈ ਕਾਹੂ ਕਉ ਦੇਤ ਨਹਿ ਨਹਿ ਭੈ ਮਾਨਤ ਆਨ ॥ ਕਹੁ ਨਾਨਕ ਸੁਨਿ ਰੇ ਮਨਾ ਗਿਆਨੀ ਤਾਹਿ ਬਖਾਨਿ ॥੧੬॥
quote.translation: One who neither frightens anyone nor is frightened by anyone — says Nanak, listen, O mind: call such a person wise.
quote.citation: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 1427 (shalok of Guru Tegh Bahadur)
quote.label: From the text (general)
quote.note: This Guru has no hymn in the Guru Granth Sahib; the verse is by Guru Tegh Bahadur and chosen to illustrate the theme, not attributed to this Guru.

stops.name: Paonta Sahib (On the Yamuna)
stops.description: Lived beside the Yamuna in Sirmur; hosted fifty-two poets, composed heroic literature and won the defensive Battle of Bhangani nearby.

quote.text: ਹੁਕਮੀ ਹੋਵਨਿ ਆਕਾਰ ਹੁਕਮੁ ਨ ਕਹਿਆ ਜਾਈ ॥
quote.translation: By His Order forms come into being; His Order cannot be put into words.
quote.label: From the text (general)
quote.note: This Guru has no hymn in the Guru Granth Sahib; the verse is by Guru Nanak and chosen to illustrate the theme, not attributed to this Guru.

stops.name: Nadaun (Beas Hills)
stops.description: Aided Kangra hill allies to resist tributary extortion along the Beas river before strengthening Anandpur’s five forts.

quote.text: ਸੂਰਾ ਸੋ ਪਹਿਚਾਨੀਐ ਜੁ ਲਰੈ ਦੀਨ ਕੇ ਹੇਤ ॥
quote.translation: He alone is known as a hero who fights for the oppressed.
quote.citation: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 1105 (Maru, Bhagat Kabir)
quote.label: From the text (general)
quote.note: This Guru has no hymn in the Guru Granth Sahib; the verse is by Bhagat Kabir and chosen to illustrate the theme, not attributed to this Guru.

stops.name: Anandpur Sahib (Birth of the Khalsa)
stops.description: Initiated the Panj Pyare with Khande-di-Pahul at Takht Kesgarh Sahib, creating the casteless Khalsa order; later endured the seven-month siege of 1704.

quote.text: ਸੂਰਾ ਸੋ ਪਹਿਚਾਨੀਐ ਜੁ ਲਰੈ ਦੀਨ ਕੇ ਹੇਤ ॥
quote.translation: He alone is known as a hero who fights for the oppressed.
quote.citation: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 1105 (Maru, Bhagat Kabir)
quote.label: From the text (general)
quote.note: This Guru has no hymn in the Guru Granth Sahib; the verse is by Bhagat Kabir and chosen to illustrate the theme, not attributed to this Guru.

stops.name: Sarsa Crossing (Parivar Vichhora)
stops.description: Winter flood in the Sarsa river separated the Guru from his mother and two younger sons Zorawar Singh and Fateh Singh (brick-martyred at Sirhind).

quote.text: ਭੈ ਕਾਹੂ ਕਉ ਦੇਤ ਨਹਿ ਨਹਿ ਭੈ ਮਾਨਤ ਆਨ ॥ ਕਹੁ ਨਾਨਕ ਸੁਨਿ ਰੇ ਮਨਾ ਗਿਆਨੀ ਤਾਹਿ ਬਖਾਨਿ ॥੧੬॥

quote.citation: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 1427 (shalok of Guru Tegh Bahadur)
quote.label: From the text (general)
quote.note: This Guru has no hymn in the Guru Granth Sahib; the verse is by Guru Tegh Bahadur and chosen to illustrate the theme, not attributed to this Guru.

stops.name: Chamkaur Sahib (Fort of Garhi)
stops.description: With forty Sikhs in a mud-walled house he held back an army; elders sons Ajit Singh and Jujhar Singh fell fighting in battle.

quote.text: ਸੂਰਾ ਸੋ ਪਹਿਚਾਨੀਐ ਜੁ ਲਰੈ ਦੀਨ ਕੇ ਹੇਤ ॥
quote.translation: He alone is known as a hero who fights for the oppressed.
quote.citation: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 1105 (Maru, Bhagat Kabir)
quote.label: From the text (general)
quote.note: This Guru has no hymn in the Guru Granth Sahib; the verse is by Bhagat Kabir and chosen to illustrate the theme, not attributed to this Guru.

stops.name: Machhiwara Forest
stops.description: Resting alone under desert scrub he composed ‘Mitra Pyare Nu’ before Pathan brothers Nabi Khan and Ghani Khan carried him out disguised as Uch da Pir.

quote.text: ਕਾਮ ਕ੍ਰੋਧ ਮਦ ਮਤਸਰ ਤ੍ਰਿਸਨਾ ਬਿਨਸਿ ਜਾਹਿ ਹਰਿ ਨਾਮੁ ਉਚਾਰੀ ॥
quote.translation: Lust, wrath, pride, jealousy and craving perish as one utters the Name of the Lord.
quote.citation: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 1389 (Guru Arjan Dev)
quote.label: From the text (general)
quote.note: This Guru has no hymn in the Guru Granth Sahib; the verse is by Guru Arjan Dev and chosen to illustrate the theme, not attributed to this Guru.

stops.name: Dina Kangar (Composition of Zafarnama)
stops.description: Wrote the Persian Zafarnama (‘Epistle of Victory’) to Emperor Aurangzeb upholding moral courage over broken oaths.

quote.text: ਸੂਰਾ ਸੋ ਪਹਿਚਾਨੀਐ ਜੁ ਲਰੈ ਦੀਨ ਕੇ ਹੇਤ ॥
quote.translation: He alone is known as a hero who fights for the oppressed.
quote.citation: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 1105 (Maru, Bhagat Kabir)
quote.label: From the text (general)
quote.note: This Guru has no hymn in the Guru Granth Sahib; the verse is by Bhagat Kabir and chosen to illustrate the theme, not attributed to this Guru.

stops.name: Khidrana / Muktsar (40 Mukte)
stops.description: Site of his final defensive victory; personally tore up the Bedava disclaimer, blessing Mai Bhago and the Forty Liberated Ones.

quote.text: ਭੈ ਕਾਹੂ ਕਉ ਦੇਤ ਨਹਿ ਨਹਿ ਭੈ ਮਾਨਤ ਆਨ ॥ ਕਹੁ ਨਾਨਕ ਸੁਨਿ ਰੇ ਮਨਾ ਗਿਆਨੀ ਤਾਹਿ ਬਖਾਨਿ ॥੧੬॥
quote.translation: One who neither frightens anyone nor is frightened by anyone — says Nanak, listen, O mind: call such a person wise.
quote.citation: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 1427 (shalok of Guru Tegh Bahadur)
quote.label: From the text (general)
quote.note: This Guru has no hymn in the Guru Granth Sahib; the verse is by Guru Tegh Bahadur and chosen to illustrate the theme, not attributed to this Guru.

stops.name: Talwandi Sabo (Damdama Sahib)
stops.description: Resting place (‘Guru ki Kashi’) where with Bhai Mani Singh he dictated the final Guru Granth Sahib text incorporating Guru Tegh Bahadur’s hymns.

quote.text: ਜੋ ਨਰੁ ਦੁਖ ਮੈ ਦੁਖੁ ਨਹੀ ਮਾਨੈ ॥
quote.translation: The person who, amid pain, does not feel pain…
quote.citation: Guru Granth Sahib, Ang 633 (Sorath, Guru Tegh Bahadur)
quote.note: Contains Guru Tegh Bahadur's hymn added into the Guru Granth Sahib at Damdama Sahib.

stops.name: Agra & Rajasthan March (Baghaur–Agra)
stops.description: Travelled across Rajasthan and met the new Mughal emperor Bahadur Shah at Agra hoping for justice against Sirhind’s governor.

quote.text: ਹੁਕਮੀ ਹੋਵਨਿ ਆਕਾਰ ਹੁਕਮੁ ਨ ਕਹਿਆ ਜਾਈ ॥
quote.translation: By His Order forms come into being; His Order cannot be put into words.
quote.label: From the text (general)
quote.note: This Guru has no hymn in the Guru Granth Sahib; the verse is by Guru Nanak and chosen to illustrate the theme, not attributed to this Guru.

stops.name: Burhanpur (Tapti River Crossing)
stops.description: Accompanied the imperial court south across the Narmada and Tapti rivers while maintaining independent Khalsa camp worship.

quote.text: ਸੋਚੈ ਸੋਚਿ ਨ ਹੋਵਈ ਜੇ ਸੋਚੀ ਲਖ ਵਾਰ ॥
quote.translation: By thinking, purity cannot be reached, though one think a hundred thousand times.
quote.label: From the text (general)
quote.note: This Guru has no hymn in the Guru Granth Sahib; the verse is by Guru Nanak and chosen to illustrate the theme, not attributed to this Guru.

stops.name: Nanded (Takht Sachkhand Sri Hazur Sahib)
stops.description: On the Godavari river, passed eternal temporal–spiritual authority to Guru Granth Sahib (‘Sab Sikhan ko hukam hai, Guru manyo Granth’) and commissioned Banda Singh Bahadur.

quote.text: ੴ ਸਤਿ ਨਾਮੁ ਕਰਤਾ ਪੁਰਖੁ ਨਿਰਭਉ ਨਿਰਵੈਰੁ ਅਕਾਲ ਮੂਰਤਿ ਅਜੂਨੀ ਸੈਭੰ ਗੁਰ ਪ੍ਰਸਾਦਿ ॥
quote.translation: There is one Being: whose name is Truth, the Creator, without fear, without enmity, of timeless form, unborn, self-existent — known by the Guru’s grace.
quote.label: From the text (general)

journeys.title: The Pandavas’ journey and battles
journeys.subtitle: From Hastinapura through the house of lac, hiding at Ekachakra, Indraprastha, exile and the eighteen-day war at Kurukshetra, to the last walk toward Mount Meru.
journeys.intro: Stops are approximate modern identifications of places named in the epic; each verse is copied from the public text linked beside it.

routes.label: The Pandavas’ route and battles
routes.summary: Fifteen stages from Hastinapura through Varanavata, Indraprastha, Digvijaya, twelve-year exile and Kurukshetra to the Himalaya.

stops.name: Kuru Kingdom (Hastinapura)
stops.description: The Pandavas grow up and train under Drona and Bhishma in the Kuru capital.

quote.text:
धर्मक्षेत्रे कुरुक्षेत्रे समवेता युयुत्सवः ।
मामकाः पाण्डवाश्चैव किमकुर्वत सञ्जय ॥
quote.translation: On the field of dharma, at Kurukshetra, assembled and eager for battle, what did my people and the sons of Pandu do, O Sanjaya?

stops.name: Varanavata (Lakshagriha)
stops.description: The house of lac is set alight; warned by Vidura, the brothers and Kunti escape through a tunnel.

quote.text: ततस्तस्मिन्पुरे लोका नगरे वारणावते। दृष्ट्वा जतुगृहं दग्धमन्वशोचन्त दुःखिताः॥
quote.translation: Then the people of the city of Varanavata, seeing the house of lac burnt, mourned in sorrow.

stops.name: Ekachakra (Hiding in disguise)
stops.description: Living disguised as mendicant Brahmins until Bhima slays the demon Bakasura. Location uncertain.

quote.text: जटाः कृत्वाऽऽत्मनः सर्वे वल्कलाजिनवाससः। कुन्त्या सह महात्मानो बिभ्रतस्तापसं वपुः॥
quote.translation: They all took on matted locks and clothing of bark and deerskin, and with Kunti the great-souled brothers bore the look of ascetics.
quote.label: From the text (general)

stops.name: Panchala (Kampilya and Ahichchhatra)
stops.description: At Draupadi’s svayamvara in Kampilya, Arjuna strings the bow and wins her hand.

quote.text:
तत्रेमे कुरुपाञ्चालाः शाल्वा माद्रेयजाङ्गलाः ।
शूरसेनाः पुलिन्दाश्च बोधा मालास्तथैव च ।
quote.translation: Here are these: the Kurus and Panchalas, the Shalvas, the Madreyas and Jangalas, the Shurasenas, Pulindas, Bodhas and Malas.
quote.citation: Mahabharata 6.9.39 (Bhishma Parva, Bhumi Parva; numbering as on sa.wikisource)

stops.name: Indraprastha
stops.description: Clearing the Khandava forest, Yudhishthira builds Indraprastha and plans the Rajasuya.

quote.text: इन्द्रप्रस्थे वसन्तस्ते त्रीणि वर्षाणि विंशतिम्। द्वादशाब्दानथैकं च बभूवुर्द्यूतनिर्जिताः॥
quote.translation: They lived at Indraprastha for three and twenty years; then, beaten at dice, they spent twelve years and one more in exile.

stops.name: Magadha
stops.description: En route to imperial sovereignty, Bhima defeats Magadhan king Jarasandha in bare-handed combat.

quote.text:
वारवास्यायवाहाश्च चक्राश्चक्रातयः शकाः।
विदेहा मगधाः स्वक्षा मलजा विजयास्तथा ।
quote.translation: The Varavasyas, Ayavahas, Chakras, Chakratayas and Shakas; the Videhas, Magadhas, Svakshas, Malajas and Vijayas.
quote.citation: Mahabharata 6.9.45 (Bhishma Parva, Bhumi Parva; numbering as on sa.wikisource)

stops.name: Pragjyotisha
stops.description: During Arjuna’s northern and eastern digvijaya campaigns he fights Bhagadatta’s mountain hosts.

quote.text:
स किरातैश्च चीनैश्च वृतः प्राग्ज्योतिषोऽभवत्।
अन्यैश्च बहुभिर्योधैः सागरानुपवासिभिः।
quote.translation: Surrounded by Kiratas and Chinas and many other warriors dwelling by the sea, he was the lord of Pragjyotisha.
quote.citation: Mahabharata 2.27.18 (Sabha Parva, Arjuna's digvijaya; numbering as on sa.wikisource)

stops.name: Manipura (Arjuna and Chitrangada's realm)
stops.description: During his twelve-month pilgrimage exile Arjuna reaches Manipura and marries Chitrangada.

quote.text: एतत्सर्वं यथावृत्तं कथितं भरतर्षभ। यथा तु स हतो राजा भीमसेनेन तच्छृणु॥
quote.translation: All this, bull among the Bharatas, has been told just as it happened; now hear how that king was slain by Bhimasena.
quote.label: From the text (general)

stops.name: Dvaraka and Anarta (Yadava realm)
stops.description: Travelling along the western seas, Arjuna reaches Dvaraka, bonds with Krishna and marries Subhadra.

quote.text:
पुण्ड्रा भर्गाः किराताश्च सुदृष्टा यामुनास्तथा।
शका निषादा निषधास्तथैवानर्तनैर्ऋताः ।
quote.translation: The Pundras, Bhargas, Kiratas, Sudrishtas and Yamunas; the Shakas, Nishadas, Nishadhas, and likewise the Anartas and Nairritas.
quote.citation: Mahabharata 6.9.51 (Bhishma Parva, Bhumi Parva; numbering as on sa.wikisource)

stops.name: Kashi
stops.description: Eastern Rajasuya alliance link before the fateful dice-match strips the brothers of their realm.

quote.text:
धृष्टकेतुश्चेकितानः काशिराजश्च वीर्यवान् ।
पुरुजित्कुन्तिभोजश्च शैब्यश्च नरपुङ्गवः ।
quote.translation: Dhrishtaketu, Chekitana, and the valiant king of Kashi; Purujit, Kuntibhoja, and Shaibya, the best of men.

stops.name: Nishada peoples and realm
stops.description: Twelve years of forest exile traversing Kamyaka, Dvaitavana, Naimisha and southern forests.

quote.text:
पुण्ड्रा भर्गाः किराताश्च सुदृष्टा यामुनास्तथा।
शका निषादा निषधास्तथैवानर्तनैर्ऋताः ।
quote.translation: The Pundras, Bhargas, Kiratas, Sudrishtas and Yamunas; the Shakas, Nishadas, Nishadhas, and likewise the Anartas and Nairritas.
quote.citation: Mahabharata 6.9.51 (Bhishma Parva, Bhumi Parva; numbering as on sa.wikisource)

stops.name: Matsya (Virata Kingdom)
stops.description: In the thirteenth year of disguise at King Virata’s court, Arjuna single-handedly repels the Kaurava cattle raid.

quote.text:
मत्स्याः कुशल्याः सौशल्याः कुंतयः कांतिकोसलाः ।
चेदिमत्स्यकरूशाश्च भोजाः सिन्धुपुलिन्दकाः ।
quote.translation: The Matsyas, Kushalyas, Saushalyas, Kuntis and Kanti-Kosalas; the Chedis, Matsyas and Karushas, the Bhojas, and the Sindhu-Pulindas.
quote.citation: Mahabharata 6.9.40 (Bhishma Parva, Bhumi Parva; numbering as on sa.wikisource)

stops.name: Kurukshetra (Dharmakshetra)
stops.description: The eighteen-day Kurukshetra war across eighteen parvas, opening with the Bhagavad Gita.

quote.text:
धर्मक्षेत्रे कुरुक्षेत्रे समवेता युयुत्सवः ।
मामकाः पाण्डवाश्चैव किमकुर्वत सञ्जय ॥
quote.translation: On the field of dharma, at Kurukshetra, assembled and eager for battle, what did my people and the sons of Pandu do, O Sanjaya?

stops.name: Kuru Kingdom (Hastinapura)
stops.description: Yudhishthira assumes the Kuru throne for thirty-six years before renouncing after Krishna’s departure.

quote.text:
धर्मक्षेत्रे कुरुक्षेत्रे समवेता युयुत्सवः ।
मामकाः पाण्डवाश्चैव किमकुर्वत सञ्जय ॥
quote.translation: On the field of dharma, at Kurukshetra, assembled and eager for battle, what did my people and the sons of Pandu do, O Sanjaya?

stops.name: Saurashtra
stops.description: Following news of the Yadava collapse near Prabhasa, the Pandavas resolve on their final departure.

quote.text: ततो युयुत्सुमानाय्य प्रव्रजन्धर्मकाम्यया। राज्यं परिददौ सर्वं वैश्यापुत्रे युधिष्ठिरः॥
quote.translation: Then, calling Yuyutsu and setting out in pursuit of dharma, Yudhishthira handed the whole kingdom over to the son of the Vaishya woman.
quote.label: From the text (general)

stops.name: Himalaya & Mount Meru (Mahaprasthana)
stops.description: Walking north across the snowy peaks toward heaven accompanied by the faithful dog.

quote.text: तं चाप्यतिक्रमन्तस्ते ददृशुर्वालुकार्णवम्। अवैक्षन्त महाशैलं मेरुं शिखरिणां वरम्॥
quote.translation: Passing beyond that, they saw an ocean of sand, and they beheld the great mountain Meru, best of peaked ranges.

journeys.title: Rama’s route: Ayodhya to Lanka and back
journeys.subtitle: From Ayodhya across the Ganga and through the Dandaka forest to Panchavati, Kishkindha, the bridge to Lanka and the return.
journeys.intro: Stops are approximate modern identifications of places named in the epic; each verse is copied from the public text linked beside it.

routes.label: Rama’s route and battles
routes.summary: Nineteen canonical stages from Bala Kanda training with Vishvamitra and Mithila’s wedding across fourteen years of exile to Lanka and the Pushpaka return.

stops.name: Ayodhya (Kosala)
stops.description: Prince Rama leaves Kosala’s capital first as Vishvamitra’s young guardian and later into exile.

quote.text:
अयोध्या नाम नगरी तत्रासील्लोकविश्रुता |
 मनुना मानवेन्द्रेण या पुरी निर्मिता स्वयम् ||
quote.translation: There was a city named Ayodhya, renowned throughout the world, which Manu, lord of humankind, had himself built.

stops.name: Sarayu River Bank
stops.description: Along the southern Sarayu bank, sage Vishvamitra imparts Bala and Atibala mantras guarding against fatigue.

quote.text: कोसलो नाम मुदितः स्फीतो जनपदो महान् | निविष्टः सरयूतीरे प्रभूतधनधान्यवान् || १-५-५
quote.translation: There is a great kingdom named Kosala, joyful and prosperous, situated on the banks of the Sarayu and rich in wealth and grain.

stops.name: Siddhashrama
stops.description: Rama defends Vishvamitra’s sacrifice, slaying Subahu and hurling Maricha into the ocean.

quote.text: अयं सिद्धाश्रमो नाम प्रसादात्ते भविष्यति | सिद्धे कर्मणि देवेश उत्तिष्ठ भगवन्नितः || १-२९-१८
quote.translation: By your grace, this place will be known as Siddhashrama. Now that the rite is complete, rise from here, lord of the gods.

stops.name: Mithila (Videha)
stops.description: Breaking Shiva’s bow in King Janaka’s assembly, Rama marries Sita before returning to Ayodhya.

quote.text: एवम् उक्तः स धर्मात्मा जनकेन महात्मना | प्रत्युवाच मुनिर् वीरम् वाक्यम् वाक्य विशारदः || १-६६-४
quote.translation: When the great-souled Janaka, ruler of Mithila, had spoken thus, the righteous, eloquent sage replied to the king.

stops.name: Tamasa River Bank
stops.description: First overnight halt after departing into exile; Ayodhya’s citizens fall asleep as the chariot drives onward.

quote.text: स तु तीरं समासाद्य तमसाया महामुनिः । शिष्यमाह स्थितं पार्श्वे दृष्ट्वा तीर्थमकर्दमम् ॥१-२-४॥
quote.translation: Having reached the bank of the Tamasa and seen a clear, mud-free bathing place, the great sage spoke to his disciple standing beside him.

stops.name: Shringaverapura (Nishada country)
stops.description: Guha, chief of the Nishadas, welcomes Rama and ferries the exiles across the Ganga.

quote.text: समुद्रमहीषीम् गङ्गाम् सारसक्रौञ्चनादिताम् | आससाद महाबाहुः शृङ्गिबेरपुरम् प्रति || २-५०-२६
quote.translation: The mighty-armed Rama reached toward Shringaverapura, where Ganga, the ocean's queen, resounded with the calls of sarasa and krauncha birds.

stops.name: Prayaga (Bharadvaja Ashrama)
stops.description: At the Ganga–Yamuna confluence, sage Bharadvaja counsels them to dwell on Chitrakuta’s forested slopes.

quote.text: प्रयागम् अभितः पश्य सौमित्रे धूमम् उन्नतम् | अग्नेर् भगवतः केतुम् मन्ये सम्निहितः मुनिः || २-५४-५
quote.translation: Look, Lakshmana, at the tall smoke near Prayaga, a sign of sacred fire; I think the sage is close by.

stops.name: Chitrakuta
stops.description: Living beside the Mandakini river; Bharata arrives to plead for Rama’s return and receives his sandals.

quote.text: अथ दाशरथिः चित्रम् चित्र कूटम् अदर्शयत् | भार्याम् अमर सम्काशः शचीम् इव पुरम् दरः
quote.translation: Then Dasharatha’s son, radiant as a god, showed his wife the wondrous Chitrakuta, as Purandara shows Shachi his city.

stops.name: Dandakaranya
stops.description: Passing through the hermitages of Atri, Sharabhanga and Sutikshna across the Vindhya forests for ten years.

quote.text:
मानुषौ शस्त्र संपन्नौ चीर कृष्ण अजिन अंबरौ |
प्रविष्टौ दण्डकारण्यम् घोरम् प्रमदया सह || ३-१९-२२
quote.translation: Two armed men, clad in bark and black deerskin, have entered the dreadful Dandaka forest with a woman.

stops.name: Agastya Ashrama
stops.description: Sage Agastya presents Vaishnava bow and quiver and directs Rama toward serene Panchavati on the Godavari.

quote.text:
स प्रविश्य आश्रम पदम् लक्ष्मणो राघव अनुजः |
अगस्त्य शिष्यम् आसाद्य वाक्यम् एतद् उवाच ह || ३-१२-१
quote.translation: Entering the hermitage, Lakshmana, Raghava's younger brother, met Agastya's disciple and spoke these words.

stops.name: Panchavati
stops.description: Hut near the Godavari river where Surpanakha provokes conflict and Ravana later carries off Sita.

quote.text:
इतो द्वि योजने तात बहु मूल फल उदकः |
देशो बहु मृगः श्रीमान् पंचवटि अभिविश्रुतः || ३-१३-१३
quote.translation: Two yojanas from here lies the famed, splendid place called Panchavati, rich in roots, fruit, water, and deer.

stops.name: Janasthana
stops.description: Rama single-handedly vanquishes fourteen thousand rakshasas led by Khara and Dushana.

quote.text:
जानीषे त्वं जनस्थानं भ्राता यत्र खरो मम ।
दूषणश्च महाबाहुः स्वसा शूर्पणखा च मे ॥
quote.translation: You know Janasthana, where my brother Khara lives, along with mighty Dushana and my sister Shurpanakha.

stops.name: Pampa Lake
stops.description: Near lotus-filled Lake Pampa and Shabari’s hermitage, Rama grieves for Sita and is pointed toward Sugriva.

quote.text:
ऋष्यमूके गिरि वरे पंपा पर्यन्त शोभिते |
निवसति आत्मवान् वीरः चतुर्भिः सह वानरैः || ३-७२-१२
quote.translation: The steadfast, heroic Sugriva dwells with four monkeys on excellent Mount Rishyamuka, made beautiful by the shores of Pampa.

stops.name: Kishkindha
stops.description: From nearby Rishyamukha Sugriva’s exile ends when Rama defeats Vali; vanara armies launch the four-way search.

quote.text:
ते गत्वा दूरमध्वानं तस्मात्सप्तजनाश्रमात् ।
ददृशुस्तां दुराधर्षां किष्किन्धां वालिपालिताम् ॥
quote.translation: After traveling far from the hermitage of the Seven Sages, they saw unconquerable Kishkindha, ruled by Vali.

stops.name: Rishyamukha Hill
stops.description: Beside the Tungabhadra hills Hanuman meets Rama and Sita’s dropped ornaments confirm the southern trail.

quote.text:
ऋष्यमूके गिरि वरे पंपा पर्यन्त शोभिते |
निवसति आत्मवान् वीरः चतुर्भिः सह वानरैः || ३-७२-१२
quote.translation: The steadfast, heroic Sugriva dwells with four monkeys on excellent Mount Rishyamuka, made beautiful by the shores of Pampa.

stops.name: Mahendra Hill
stops.description: Sundara Kanda summit above the eastern coast where Hanuman leaps south across the sea to discover Sita.

quote.text: पीड्यमानस्तु बलिना महेन्द्रस्तेन पर्वतः | रीतीर्निर्वर्तयामास काञ्चनाञ्जनराजतीः
quote.translation: Pressed down by the mighty one, Mount Mahendra poured out streams of ore, gold, collyrium and silver.

stops.name: Rameshwaram and the Setu
stops.description: Nala and the vanara army engineer the stone causeway linking the southern cape toward Lanka.

quote.text:
एष सेतुम् महाउत्साहः करोतु मयि वानरः |
तम् अहम् धारयिष्यामि तथा हि एष यथा पिता || ६-२२-४५
quote.translation: Let this greatly energetic monkey build a bridge across me; I shall support it, for he is like his father.

stops.name: Lanka
stops.description: Yuddha Kanda triumph: Kumbhakarna, Indrajit and Ravana fall; Sita is rescued and Vibhishana crowned.

quote.text:
स सागरमनाधृष्यमतिक्रम्य महाबलः |
त्रिकूटशिखरे लङ्कां स्थितां स्वस्थो ददर्श ह || ५-२-१
quote.translation: Having crossed the impassable ocean, the mighty Hanuman saw Lanka situated on the summit of Trikuta, still in full strength.

stops.name: Ayodhya (Kosala)
stops.description: Aerial return aboard the Pushpaka chariot for Rama’s Rajyabhisheka crowning beside Sita.

quote.text:
अयोध्या नाम नगरी तत्रासील्लोकविश्रुता |
 मनुना मानवेन्द्रेण या पुरी निर्मिता स्वयम् ||
quote.translation: There was a city named Ayodhya, renowned throughout the world, which Manu, lord of humankind, had himself built.
